1|# Changelog
2|
3|All notable changes to trimtok are documented here.
4|
5|## [4.3.0] - 2026-10-27
6|
7|Real savings on traffic that used to pass through untouched, measured on a real
8|corpus (`eval/`, 32 payloads / 1.13MB, no mocks): **60.45% -> 72.45%** with zero
9|accuracy-gate failures (was 2 before this release).
10|
11|### Added
12|- **Structural fold for non-code `read_file` payloads.** The only structural lane
13|  was a Python AST skeleton, so markdown / yaml / rst / jsonl fell through to a
14|  verbatim passthrough (`reason=below_skeleton_min`) — 16.6% of all production
15|  tokens at ~1.5% saving. `pruners.fold_text_structure` keeps headings, fences,
16|  tables and key lines with their exact original `LINE|` prefix and replaces prose
17|  runs with a marker naming the real line range (`[tt:prose L120-L138 (19L)]`), so
18|  a patch by offset still works. Records are never swallowed whole: the first line
19|  of every distinct JSON key shape survives. Code extensions are deliberately
20|  excluded. Corpus effect: README 0->39.6%, CHANGELOG 0->66.5%, skill files
21|  0->51-72%, usage.jsonl 0->97.4% (11 distinct record shapes kept).
22|- **`tests/test_real_corpus.py`** — 243 assertions over every corpus payload,
23|  driven through the real entry points. Asserts no exception escapes, no payload
24|  inflates, every added `#ref` resolves in the CCR, dropped fault lines are
25|  announced, prose ranges stay inside the file, headings and top-level symbols
26|  survive. Refuses to touch `~/.trimtok` (temp data dir) and runs in ~1.4s.
27|
28|### Fixed
29|- **Fault lines were hidden without saying so.** With more fault lines than the
30|  window budget, `_window` kept the *first* `budget` of them, so every later error
31|  vanished silently — the errors that end a run live at the tail. It now samples
32|  the fault set evenly and always keeps its tail, and the header carries
33|  `errors_hidden=K` (tier 0 is forced up to tier 2 so the count is never lost).
34|  Masked faults were counted by multiset, not by set: five identical errors with
35|  one kept used to report zero hidden.
36|- **A 435KB log was killed by its own guard and shipped raw.** The 200ms guard was
37|  applied regardless of payload size, so a 435KB log (222ms of honest work) went
38|  out at 0% saved. The guard now scales with size above 100KB (capped at 3x), and
39|  a genuine timeout still ships the ANSI-stripped text instead of the raw payload.
40|- **Passthrough gates named themselves but carried no `reason`**
41|  (`passthrough_small`, `passthrough_sentinel`), so consumers could not tell a
42|  size cutoff from a sentinel skip.
43|
44|## [4.2.6] - 2026-10-26
45|
46|Measurement honesty + the real hot path. No compression algorithm changed.
47|
48|### Fixed
49|- **usage.jsonl reported passthrough gates as 100% saved.** `after_chars` was
50|  written as 0 for every passthrough gate, so any aggregate of
51|  `1 - after/before` counted ~2.6M untouched tokens as fully eliminated. The
52|  published headline (48.5% terminal / 38.7% tool) was inflated ~3.5x; real
53|  production values over 4,323 events are **13.7% terminal / 7.5% tool (9.5%
54|  overall)**. Passthrough rows now record `after == before`.
55|- **`_classify` / `_ERROR_RE` cost 42us per 70-char line.** The `looks_suspicious`
56|  prefilter carried loose hints ("status", "sig", "memory", "http") so every
57|  info log line reached the 614-char case-insensitive alternation. A 20,000-line
58|  dump took 1.3s of pure regex (and blew the fail-open deadline). The prefilter
59|  now asserts the literal prefix first (`_STATUS5_RE`, `_HTTP5_RE`,
60|  `_HEX_FRAME_RE`) and stays a strict superset of `_ERROR_RE`: 0 rejected lines
61|  out of 88,890 that the regex would match. `_classify` 1206ms -> 118ms on
62|  20,000 lines; a 1.56MB payload compresses in 163ms instead of 751ms.
63|- **`OOMKilled` and `npm ERR!` were not detected as fault lines** and could be
64|  folded away.
65|
66|### Changed
67|- **`guard_ms` default 50 -> 200.** Real p99 is 63ms, worst observed 145ms; at 50
68|  every payload over ~9K tokens hit the deadline and saved nothing (20 events /
69|  188,686 tokens in the sample). The deadline is still fail-open.
70|- **Gate reasons are recorded** (`reason` in usage.jsonl): `small`,
71|  `targeted_slice`, `anti_poison`, `below_skeleton_min`, `no_gain_fold`,
72|  `header_cost`, `deadline`, `sentinel`, plus the exception text. The
73|  `passthrough_reference` gate has four distinct causes and was indistinguishable
74|  in telemetry.
75|- **`shape="ref-verbatim"`** for the read_file passthrough band, which previously
76|  hid 14.7% of all tokens inside `shape="mixed"`.
77|- **Tests no longer write production telemetry.** Mocked-gate rows (`gate="small"`,
78|  fixtures like `git statusx`) polluted the real usage.jsonl and skewed every
79|  real-world number.
80|
81|## [4.2.3] - 2026-10-24
82|
83|### Changed
84|- **Zero Model / Zero Daemon Architecture Documentation**:
85|  - Re-affirmed standalone context compression architecture: operates 100% via heuristic AST analysis, BPE token estimation, differential patching, and lossless Zstandard CCR caching.
86|  - Requires zero embedding models, zero GPU/ONNX runtimes, zero external daemons, and zero network calls.
87|  - Hardened cross-platform SQLite WAL concurrency and file-locking on Windows NTFS.
88|
89|## [4.2.2] - 2026-10-21
90|
91|The v4.2 stateful read-file lane never fired in real Hermes: 1,078 `read_file`
92|calls / 5.83M characters were passed through with 0% reduction. Argon 4 reviewed
93|the code and confirmed the root cause plus four more co-killers; all five are
94|fixed here. `tests/test_v422_hermes_read_lane.py` reproduces the real runtime
95|(`offset=1, limit=2000` defaults and `LINE|CONTENT` payloads) and was verified
96|to fail against the pre-fix code.
97|
98|### Fixed
99|- **Hermes' default pagination no longer defeats the engine** (`trimtok/dedup.py`) -
100|  Hermes always sends `offset=1, limit=2000`, so the old Rule 0 rejected every
101|  call as a "targeted slice". A read is now treated as targeted only when it
102|  really starts inside the file (`offset > 1`, first line number > 1) or when the
103|  caller deliberately capped a small window - decided from the payload and the
104|  arguments alone, without touching the filesystem.
105|- **Numbered payloads are unwrapped before analysis** (`trimtok/dedup.py`,
106|  `trimtok/pruners.py`) - Hermes returns every line as `LINE|CONTENT`, which
107|  broke `ast.parse()`, the outline detector and the line-number diff. The
108|  payload is unwrapped to raw source, analysed there, and the original `LINE|`
109|  prefixes are re-attached to every kept line; skeleton markers now carry the
110|  real file line numbers.
111|- **The file cache survives a patch** (`trimtok/dedup.py`) - the mutating-tool
112|  handler dropped the cached body, so the contextual-delta lane could never fire
113|  in a real read -> patch -> re-read loop. The body is now kept and flagged.
114|- **The file cache survives multi-step agent loops** (`trimtok/dedup.py`) -
115|  `expire_old_turns` aged file bodies out after two tool steps; they now live
116|  for eight, matching how long a read -> search -> terminal -> read loop runs.
117|- **`read_file_extra` reaches the engine** (`trimtok/dedup.py`,
118|  `trimtok/signals.py`, `trimtok/__init__.py`) - the second Hermes read tool was
119|  dropped by a hardcoded tool-name check, and read tools are no longer treated
120|  as verbatim-only.
121|
122|### Added
123|- **Anti-loop rail** (`trimtok/dedup.py`) - a re-read that already received a stub
124|  or a skeleton returns the real file instead of another pointer.
125|- **Cheap token gate** (`trimtok/dedup.py`) - the BPE pass only runs when the
126|  candidate is close in size to the original; the char ratio already proves the
127|  token count dropped otherwise.
128|- **Fail-open on the guard budget** (`trimtok/dedup.py`) - a file read that is
129|  out of time ships the verbatim file instead of blowing the deadline.
130|- **Work log** (`reports/CHANGELOG_TH.md`) - one living changelog per topic with
131|  the measured numbers; the raw Argon reviews live in `reports/raw/`.
132|
133|### Measured
134|- `read_file` cold-read band: 240,202 -> 115,155 characters (52.1% reduction;
135|  0% before) - benchmark `RESULT: PASS`, all acceptance gates met.
136|- Test suite: 31 passed (27 previous + 4 new Hermes-fidelity tests).
137|- Latency, read_file band: p50 6.49 ms, p95 74.83 ms (43 KB file).
138|
139|## [4.2.1] - 2026-10-21
140|
141|Argon 4 reviewed the v4.2 diff in the original planning thread and returned
142|**REQUEST CHANGES** with five blockers. All five are fixed here, and each fix has
143|a regression test (`tests/test_v42_argon_fixes.py`) that was verified to fail
144|against the pre-fix code.
145|
146|### Fixed
147|- **Syntax corruption in the AST skeletonizer** (`trimtok/pruners.py`) - a method
148|  whose docstring was followed by a blank line read its indentation from that
149|  blank line and emitted `pass` at the wrong depth (`IndentationError`), and a
150|  nested decorated `def` left its `@decorator` above the `pass` (`SyntaxError`).
151|  The indentation now comes from the first folded statement, a nested decorator
152|  is folded with its `def`, and the fold range stays contiguous so the retrieval
153|  coordinates in the marker still match the file.
154|- **A re-read after a cold skeleton no longer lies** (`trimtok/dedup.py`) - the
155|  first read of a file over 12 KB returns a skeleton; the next read used to answer
156|  "identical to prior read in active context" with an outline even though the
157|  agent had never seen the body. The cache now records that only a skeleton was
158|  delivered, and a repeat read returns the real file.
159|- **A unified diff is no longer corrupted** (`trimtok/core.py`, `trimtok/dedup.py`) -
160|  `hygiene()` stripped the single space that a diff context line carries, and the
161|  512-2047 char band skipped the clean path whenever the payload had repeated
162|  lines. Diff payloads now skip `hygiene()` entirely, and a payload with repeated
163|  lines is folded and marked instead of being dropped to a passthrough.
164|- **The adaptive tool header is wired in** (`trimtok/dedup.py`, `trimtok/signals.py`) -
165|  `compress_tool_result` used the fixed v4.1 header with no token gate and no
166|  rescue. It now scales the header by the saving, gates on real token counts, and
167|  downgrades to the nano header before reverting. The tier order was also
168|  corrected: Tier 2 was longer than Tier 3.
169|- **Shell mutations invalidate the cached body** (`trimtok/core.py`) -
170|  `invalidate_shell_mutations` was written but never called, so a `git checkout`
171|  or `sed -i` left a stale "file unchanged" entry behind.
172|- **Cached file bodies now expire with their turn** (`trimtok/dedup.py`,
173|  `trimtok/__init__.py`) - `expire_old_turns` marked the fold index but not the
174|  file cache, and a verbatim read was never noted, so a file could be served as
175|  "unchanged" long after it had left the context window.
176|- **The delta header now advertises a retrievable ref** (`trimtok/dedup.py`) -
177|  `#prev_ref` pointed at content that was never written to the CCR, so
178|  `trimtok_retrieve` on it failed with "Not found or expired".
179|
180|### Added
181|- `tests/test_v42_argon_fixes.py` - eight regression tests, one per blocker plus
182|  the contract checks that must keep holding.
183|
184|### Changed
185|- The read-file delta path is limited to files of at most 1500 lines; above that
186|  the file is skeletonized instead, because `SequenceMatcher` on lines does not
187|  fit the guard budget.
188|
189|## [4.2.0] - 2026-10-20
190|
191|### Added
192|- **Three-Tier Stateful File Engine (`trimtok/dedup.py`)**:
193|  - Implemented `_handle_read_file_v42` to eliminate the 0% compression bottleneck on `read_file` (1,107 calls, 5,966,692 characters previously passed through uncompressed across 9,303 telemetry events).
194|  - Tier 1 (Unchanged Repeat): Emits a content-addressed reference stub (`[tt:file_unchanged #digest]`) with a structural AST outline when file content is identical across turns within active context.
195|  - Tier 2 (Mutated Re-Read): Emits a contextual line-numbered delta displaying modified hunks with plus-or-minus 15 lines of surrounding context when a file is edited and re-read.
196|  - Tier 3 (Cold Oversize Read): Skeletonizes cold files exceeding 12,000 characters using line-anchored body folds, while files under 12,000 characters and targeted reads (`offset`/`limit`) remain 100% verbatim for single-turn patch safety.
197|  - Added deterministic file cache invalidation on file mutation tools (`patch`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `replace_in_file`, `apply_patch`, `multi_edit`) and shell modification commands (`git checkout`, `git reset`, `sed -i`).
198|- **Line-Anchored Smart AST Skeletonizer (`trimtok/pruners.py`)**:
199|  - Implemented `smart_skeletonize_code` using pure Python standard library `ast.parse`.
200|  - Preserves 100% of imports, module-level constants, decorators, complete function signatures, type annotations, first docstring lines, and terminal return/raise statements.
201|  - Retains functions of 15 lines or fewer completely verbatim; folds longer bodies into valid Python syntax comment stubs with exact 1-indexed line coordinates (`Lstart-Lend`) and content-addressed `#cN` retrieval references.
202|- **Four-Tier Adaptive Header Scaling (`trimtok/signals.py`)**:
203|  - Added `adaptive_terminal_head` and `adaptive_tool_head` to dynamically scale marker overhead based on payload size and net character savings.
204|  - Tier 0: Headerless output (`0 chars` / `0 tokens`) for lossless operations with zero hidden or dropped lines.
205|  - Tier 1: Nano header (`[tt:#c1 -18L]`, 13–16 chars / ~4 tokens) for payloads 500 to 4,096 chars or savings under 240 chars.
206|  - Tier 2: Compact one-line header (`48–68 chars` / `~14 tokens`) for payloads 4,097 to 8,192 chars with savings of 240 chars or more.
207|  - Tier 3: Full diagnostic header and legend (`160–180 chars` / `~48 tokens`) for payloads exceeding 8,192 chars.
208|  - Added Cascade Gate Rescue: automatically downscales header tiers (Tier 3 to Tier 1 to Tier 0) before rejecting candidates, targeting a reduction of the 6.0% `reverted_gate` failure rate (558 events) to under 0.8%.
209|- **Sub-Millisecond Micro-Minification Fast Lane (`trimtok/dedup.py`, `trimtok/core.py`)**:
210|  - Implemented `micro_minify_tool` and terminal micro-minification for payloads in the 512 to 2,047 character band (previously bypassed as `passthrough_small` across 1,306 events or 24.1% of telemetry).
211|  - Performs lossless ANSI stripping, whitespace and blank-line hygiene, in-memory JSON minification, and adjacent repeat folding (>= 4 lines) in under 0.25 ms without header bloat.
212|- **Telemetry Acceptance Verification Suite (`tests/test_v42_telemetry_gates.py`)**:
213|  - Added verification test suite asserting 100% fault preservation, AST syntax validity, multi-turn file lifecycle compression, elimination of 2KB–3KB `reverted_gate` failures, and sub-millisecond micro-minification latency.
214|
215|### Changed
216|- **Pipeline Tool Argument Propagation (`trimtok/__init__.py`)**:
217|  - Updated `_on_tool_result` to forward invocation arguments (`args`) to `compress_tool_result`, enabling file path, offset, and limit awareness in downstream dedup handlers.
218|- **CCR Storage Optimization (`trimtok/__init__.py`)**:
219|  - Bypassed SQLite CCR disk persistence for `lossless_tier0` operations where no content lines are hidden or dropped, reducing unnecessary disk I/O and database lock contention.
220|- **Turn Masking Expiration (`trimtok/dedup.py`)**:
221|  - Updated `expire_old_turns` to mark cached file entries as expired when they exceed `mask_keep_turns`, preventing stale file references to contents no longer in context.
222|
223|### Fixed
224|- **Repeated Tool Output Short-Circuit (`trimtok/dedup.py`)**:
225|  - Fixed `raw_hashes` bug where identical tool results across turns triggered `passthrough_repeat` and emitted uncompressed raw text; separated failed hashes (`failed_raw`) from active span tracking so repeated identical outputs fold correctly into `[tt:seen N lines #c1]`.
226|- **Post-implementation review fixes (verified against the v4.1.0 baseline):**
227|  - `NameError: raw_hashes` — two leftover `raw_hashes.add()` calls survived the rewrite, so *every* large tool result returned `passthrough_exception` and compression was silently dead. The failed-hash path now records into `failed_hashes`; the success-path add is gone.
228|  - `passthrough_exception` now carries the exception type and message in the stats dict. A swallowed exception here disables all tool-result compression and was previously invisible in telemetry.
229|  - Unchanged-repeat stub hint shortened (`Outline (read_file offset/limit for exact lines):`), which brings the cache-hit lane from 79.6% to >80% saved.
230|  - `micro_minify_tool` no longer calls `estimate_tokens()` (a real BPE pass, ~0.19 ms per 1.6 KB, twice per call). The lane gates on character reduction instead, taking p95 from 0.39 ms to 0.12 ms against the 0.25 ms target.
231|  - Exact-repeat results are now re-compressed rather than passed through raw (the old path re-sent the whole payload); `tests/test_benchmark.py` asserts the new "smaller, never larger" contract.
232|
233|## [4.1.0] - 2026-10-20
234|
235|### Added
236|- **PyPI Release Workflow** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): automated build, twine verification, and Trusted Publishing to PyPI on GitHub release.
237|- **Hermes Plugin Entry Point Fix** (`__init__.py`): re-exported `register` attribute on the root module object so host loaders that maintain namespaced module references can locate `register` directly.
238|
239|## [4.0.0] - 2026-10-18
240|
241|### Added
242|- **Universal Stdio MCP Server & Multi-Client Installer (`mcp_server.py`, `mcp_install.py`, `__main__.py`)**:
243|  - Exposes `trimtok_compress_terminal`, `trimtok_compress_tool`, `trimtok_retrieve`, and `trimtok_status` over newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 (`msgspec`-accelerated when available).
244|  - One-command `trimtok install` / `trimtok clients` / `trimtok uninstall` auto-registers across Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Antigravity IDE, OpenAI Codex CLI, OpenCode, and VS Code (GitHub Copilot).
245|- **Direct On-Disk `file_path` Compression (`mcp_server.py`)**:
246|  - `trimtok_compress_terminal` and `trimtok_compress_tool` now accept an optional `file_path` argument to read, compress/skeletonize, and cache large log files, JSON payloads, or source code directly from disk without loading raw bytes into the LLM context window first.
247|- **Zero-Willpower Agent Habit & MCP Instructions (`SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS`)**:
248|  - Returns `instructions` in the MCP `initialize` handshake and automatically provisions `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp/trimtok/instructions.md` plus `~/.skill-proof/skills/trimtok/SKILL.md` during `trimtok install`.
249|- **AST Code Skeletonization & Zstandard CCR v3 (`code_skeleton.py`, `ccr.py`)**:
250|  - Structural AST folding for large source files alongside TOON v2 tabular JSON encoding and SQLite WAL + Zstandard blob storage.
251|
252|## [3.0.0] - 2026-10-16
253|
254|### Added
255|- **True-BPE Token Gate & Fast Ingestion (`bpe_estimator.py`)**: Singleton offline `tiktoken` (cl100k_base / o200k_base) and Rust `jiter` fast parser with seamless Python stdlib fallbacks. Non-inflation token gate actively blocks token bloating.
256|- **TOON v2 Hierarchical & Nested Columnar Codec (`toon_codec.py`)**: Dot-notation unnesting for wrapper payloads (`@data.results[N]{fields}:`), compact inline JSON cells for small lists/dicts (<= 120 chars), and recursive in-memory type-strict equality without string serialization. Achieves 70–78% reduction on nested tool results.
257|- **Two-Stage Fuzzy Stateful Delta Engine (`delta_engine.py`)**: Safe command family normalization (strips cosmetic `-v`, `-q`, `--tb=...` flags while preserving scope/targets like `-k`), $O(N)$ skeleton match (`_skeleton`) for shifted line numbers/timestamps, and `rapidfuzz` fuzzy line alignment. Preserves recurring faults in `STILL FAILING` (98.5% token reduction).
258|- **Structured Traceback & Semantic Diff Pruning (`traceback_pruner.py`, `diff_engine.py`)**: Collapses intermediate framework frames in Python and Node/JS while preserving 100% of entrypoints, user frames, crash sites, and exception lines. Evaluated before classifier to guarantee harmony with Quality Gate (zero `reverted_quality`). Diff engine preserves file headers, hunk headers with scope, and change lines while collapsing middle context.
259|- **Targeted Context-Aware CCR v3 Section Retrieval (`__init__.py`)**: Read-time slicing in `trimtok_retrieve` supporting `section="errors"`, `"diff"`, `"summary"`, `"tail"`, with configurable `context_lines` (default 3), achieving >77% token savings on retrieval without touching SQLite schema.
260|- Comprehensive test suite `tests/test_v3_upgrade.py` with 86 new checks, bringing test coverage to 376 checks (10 suites, 100% PASS, 0 FAIL).
261|
262|## [0.10.0] - 2026-10-15
263|
264|### Added
265|- Cross-turn command delta engine: a repeated terminal command (pytest, git status, git diff) whose output overlaps the previous run by at least 65% collapses to an Added / Removed / STILL FAILING view. Per-session LRU state, snapshots stored lazily so refs resolve, 0.61 ms median delta step on the 200-line class.
266|- STILL FAILING rail: a fault present in both runs is always re-emitted (regression blindness canary); newly failing lines are ordered faults-first.
267|
268|### Changed
269|- Fault classification memoized (LRU, short lines): repeat scans of a 2,000-line output drop from about 10 ms to about 1.3 ms.
270|- Command delta refs always resolve to store aliases (`#cN`) in the packaged plugin.
271|
272|### Fixed
273|- The packaged plugin no longer builds a second `ccr_v2` module instance (previously caused transient lock errors that degraded refs to raw hashes, plus a leaked sqlite handle). The runtime test now asserts alias refs.
274|
275|## [0.9.0] - 2026-10-15
276|
277|### Added
278|- Lossless JSON to TOON columnar codec: type-strict round-trip verification gates every fold, and a fold applies only with at least 4 BPE tokens of net gain (Token-Gain Gate). A 1,000-row JSON table shrinks by 74.3%.
279|
280|## [0.8.0] - 2026-10-15
281|
282|### Added
283|- Fault-polarity single source (`polarity.py`) with HTTP 5xx coverage: `status=500`, `HTTP/1.1 502`, `bad gateway`.
284|- Scoped search grouping: multi-file grep results group per file with definition headers.
285|
286|### Fixed
287|- Template folds can no longer swallow a fault line inside a repeated block.
288|

293|- Fail-open deadline guard (`guard_ms`, default 50 ms): a hook that exceeds its budget returns the original text.

300|- In-memory LRU tier for the retrieval store.

302|## [0.6.1] - 2026-10-13
303|
304|### Fixed
305|- `/trimtok` registered through `ctx.register_command` (the previous call target did not exist on the host).

307|## [0.6.0] - 2026-10-13
308|
309|### Added
310|- Drain-style template fold (`×N` plus a verbatim sample), shingle near-dedup (Jaccard at least 0.8), HEAD_TAIL stubs for large unique documents, the `marker.py` module, usage logging, and a quality gate with partial overflow mode.

315|## [0.5.2] - 2026-10-12
316|
317|### Added
318|- `trimtok_retrieve` pagination and regex filtering, balanced windowing, single-pass CCR eviction, session lifecycle memory reclamation, and opt-out controls with runtime coverage.

320|## [0.5.0] - 2026-10-11
321|
322|### Added
323|- Initial release: terminal reduction (ANSI strip, adjacent-repeat fold, balanced windowing, per-command budgets), cross-turn tool-result fold, and the content-addressed retrieval cache.
324|
